01 — The Workshop

One maker. One workshop. Nothing off a shelf.

Drape Expectations is run by Claire from her workshop in Gloucestershire. With over 20 years' experience in needlework and drapery, she maintains designer standards in everything that leaves the bench — each piece is cut, sewn and finished by hand, only when you order it.

“I have over 20 years experience in needlework and drapery. I am based in Gloucestershire and I always maintain designer standards.”

Her creations range from curtains — simple to elaborate — and blinds, plain to intricate, to cushions, personalised cot sets and nursery items, baby rompers, bloomers, coats, dresses and leggings, through to small gifts. If you have something in mind that isn't on the site, Claire will gladly work with you to create it.

Advice and quotations are free — just ask. There is also a range of ready-made clothing to browse in the shop.

— Claire

The Measuring Guide

How to measure for your new curtains

To ensure the perfect fit — whether bespoke, made-to-measure or readymade — the measurements you provide must be exact. Two dimensions are needed to manufacture your curtains: Width and Drop. Use a steel tape; plastic tapes can stretch.

A

Drop A

Finishing 1cm above your window sill.

B

Drop B

Finishing 15–20cm below your window sill.

C

Drop C

Finishing 2cm above your radiator.

D

Drop D

Finishing 1cm above your floor finish.

Width

The width measurement should be the length of your pole or track. For poles, this should not include finials.

  • New poles: allow an additional 15cm either side of the edge of your window (your window's reveal).
  • Track: the full length of the track.
  • Pole: the full length of the pole, NOT including finials.

Drop

  • Always measure from the top of the track.
  • For Pencil Pleat and Pinch Pleat headings, measure from the bottom of the underside of the pole ring, so the pole can be seen above the curtain.
  • For Tab Top or Eyelet curtains, measure from the top of the pole (ignoring finials) — exactly as you would for a track.
  • Measure at least 3 different positions across the width, and use the shortest — this avoids curtains dragging on radiators, sills or the floor.

If you should require any further guidance, please feel free to contact Claire.
